title: Forum-selection clauses
summary: An agreement identifies where the parties will litigate covered disputes.
notes: Keep formation, notice, scope, enforceability, and the procedural mechanism of enforcement distinct.

sections.Civil Procedure explanation:
A forum-selection clause is an agreement designating the court or place where specified disputes are to be litigated. Its scope, enforceability, and procedural effect require separate questions.

Read whether the clause is exclusive, which claims and parties it covers, and what law governs enforcement. Compare Bremen and Carnival on enforcement and Atlantic Marine on how a valid clause affects transfer in federal court.

A forum clause differs from a choice-of-law clause. Agreement also does not create missing federal subject-matter jurisdiction. Carnival’s notice concession must not be converted into a general holding that every passenger had adequate notice.
